title: Definition of Multi-Parameter Super-Resolution for Optical Telescopes
abstract: Super-resolution techniques in microscopy are opening new frontiers in biology, and super-resolution for telescope imaging may provide similar benefits for astronomy and space domain awareness. Telescope super-resolution techniques such as multi-plane light conversion and photonic lanterns have been inspired by the ability of mode sorting measurements to extract classical Fisher information closer to the quantum bound than standard telescope imaging. Fisher information analyses for super-resolution imaging systems commonly consider the case of imaging point sources, but often only consider estimating a small subset of the parameters. Furthermore, there has been no demonstration of an estimation algorithm with performance that follows the limit set by the Fisher information when all point source parameters are considered. We provide a framework for defining and analyzing super-resolution using the classical and quantum Fisher information for the multi-parameter estimation problem and demonstrate an algorithm that can achieve the classical Fisher information bound for all the parameters simultaneously.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a Fisher-information-based framework to define and analyze multi-parameter super-resolution for optical telescope imaging and demonstrates an estimation algorithm that simultaneously achieves the classical Fisher information bound for all point-source parameters.
summaries.zh: 本文提出了基于Fisher信息的框架，用于定义与分析光学望远镜的多参数超分辨成像，并展示一种估计算法可同时达到对所有点源参数的经典Fisher信息上限。

title: Fast local field calculation in cascaded coupled systems
abstract: Computing the field within a sub-unit of cascaded systems is a recurring problem in wave physics. It is central to gradient-based inverse design, in situations where only a region of the system is modified while the rest remains fixed. Standard approaches either resimulate the entire cascade at every change, or require a detailed characterization of every surrounding sub-system. Both become impractical when many design iterations are needed. Here, we introduce a hybrid method combining the $S$-matrix approach, which propagates fields through cascaded systems, with the Green's function method, which gives the field generated by a source within a characterized system. In this approach, the sub-systems surrounding the region of interest need only be characterized once, after which the local field can be recomputed rapidly for any new configuration. We validate the method on a disordered lossy waveguide, finding excellent agreement with finite-element simulations. We also demonstrate its efficiency on a disordered multimode cavity, where it achieves a fifty-fold speed-up over full-wave simulation and reduces a wideband focusing calculation from eleven hours to ten minutes. This approach opens the way to fast, iterative field calculations in complex systems coupled to their environment, with direct applications to inverse design and wideband wavefront-shaping.

summaries.en: The paper presents a hybrid S-matrix/Green’s-function method to efficiently recompute the local field inside a modified sub-unit of a cascaded, coupled wave system by characterizing surrounding sub-systems once, achieving close agreement with finite-element results and up to a 50× speed-up over full-wave simulation for disordered multimode cavities and wideband focusing.
summaries.zh: 本文提出一种结合S矩阵与格林函数的混合方法，通过仅对感兴趣区域周围的子系统进行一次表征，就能在级联耦合波系统中对被修改子单元的局部场进行快速重算；结果在含散射损耗波导中与有限元仿真高度一致，并在含散射多模腔与宽带聚焦计算中相对全波仿真实现最高约50倍加速，显著将计算时间从11小时降至10分钟。

title: A Portable Optical Frequency Comb with Low Repetition-Rate Drift Based on "Optical Cubes"
abstract: We demonstrate a compact, fully stabilized, all-polarization-maintaining (all-PM) Er:fiber optical frequency comb (OFC) implemented on a silica optical-cube platform. The optical comb module, including the oscillator, amplifier, spectral-broadening stage, 780-nm frequency-doubling branch, and f-to-2f interferometer, occupies a volume of 0.88 L. Without active temperature control, the free-running repetition frequency exhibits a peak-to-peak excursion of 75 Hz over 10 h, corresponding to 0.375 ppm. Under the same laboratory conditions, this excursion is 6.2 times smaller than that of a mechanically mounted non-PM reference comb. The amplified pulses are compressed to 94 fs and spectrally broadened in a PM highly nonlinear fiber. A coherent-population-trapping-based chip-scale atomic clock is employed for the first time as the radio-frequency reference for comb locking, thereby reducing the footprint of the microwave-reference subsystem. The resulting in-loop, optical-frequency-normalized tracking instability reaches 6.03E-17 at 1 s and 2.57E-18 at 10,000 s. These results demonstrate a compact comb architecture with reduced sensitivity to environmental perturbations, providing a practical route toward portable optical atomic clocks.

summaries.en: The paper reports a compact, fully stabilized all-PM Er:fiber optical frequency comb on a silica optical-cube platform with low repetition-rate drift, chip-scale atomic-clock RF referencing, and demonstrated optical-frequency-normalized tracking instability of 6.

title: Near-focus intensity evolution of spatiotemporal optical vortex pulses and consequences for their nonlinear upconversion
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortex (STOV) laser pulses are attracting attention for their puzzling transverse orbital angular momentum (OAM) and propagation properties, which could determine their future applications. While the characteristic reshaping of their space-time envelope upon diffraction from the focal plane to the far-field is now well-established, the evolution of their intensity as they propagate has not been studied quantitatively, despite growing interest for their use in nonlinear optics and strong-field physics. Here, we explore experimentally and analytically the focusing dynamics of STOVs produced by a pulse shaper, and evidence a substantial longitudinal shift between the coordinate at which a circularly-symmetric STOV forms and that at which the pulse reaches its peak intensity. To illustrate some practical consequences for applications, we experimentally demonstrate how the yield of second-harmonic generation can consequently be maximized several Rayleigh lengths beyond the plane where the circular STOV really occurs. These results signal careful characterization of spatiotemporal pulses as a requisite for nonlinear optical experiments, and pave the way for finer control of complex laser drivers for light-matter interactions.

summaries.en: The paper experimentally and analytically studies the focusing dynamics of spatiotemporal optical vortex pulses, showing a significant longitudinal displacement between where a circularly symmetric STOV forms and where the pulse attains peak intensity, which is then used to maximize second-harmonic generation several Rayleigh lengths after that formation plane.
summaries.zh: 本文通过实验与解析研究时空光学涡旋脉冲的聚焦动力学，发现其形成圆对称STOV的位置与脉冲达到峰值强度的位置之间存在显著的纵向偏移，并进一步表明可利用这一效应在该STOV形成平面之后若干瑞利长度处最大化二次谐波产生。

title: Selective spatiotemporal mode-locking in multimode Mamyshev oscillators
abstract: Spatiotemporal mode-locking (STML) in multimode fibers introduces spatial degrees of freedom for ultrashort pulse generation, yet flexible manipulation of transverse mode compositions within multimode solitons remains challenging. Here, we propose a spectrum-to-mode mapping strategy in multimode Mamyshev oscillators (MOs) to selectively synchronize specific transverse modes through synergistic cross-phase modulation and offset spectral filtering. Meanwhile, four-wave mixing acts to stabilize intermodal phase relationships, facilitating selective STML characterized by diverse mode compositions with matched group velocities. Spatiotemporal solitons containing the pure LP01 mode, degenerate LP11 modes, or LP02+LP21 composite modes are selectively realized and mapped across the parameter space spanned by intracavity gain and filter detuning. Furthermore, intracavity collisions between coexisting mode groups with disparate group velocities are demonstrated to enable dynamic mode selection. Beyond the simulation of six modes in graded-index multimode fibers, selective STML is also demonstrated in MOs based on step-index multimode fibers and fibers supporting more transverse modes, confirming the generality of our approach. This strategy offers a versatile and robust pathway for transverse mode regulation and provides new insights into full dimensional structured light manipulation in multimode ultrafast fiber lasers.

title: Ultra-low-loss Ta2O5 waveguide for integrated nonlinear photonics
abstract: Integrated nonlinear photonics demands waveguides that simultaneously offer ultra-low-loss, relatively strong nonlinearity, and tight mode confinement. Tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) is attractive for this purpose because it combines a broad transparency window, relatively strong third-order nonlinearity, and favorable thick-film growth characteristics. In tightly confined Ta2O5 waveguides, however, enhanced interaction between the optical mode and etched sidewalls makes scattering loss an important limitation for achieving high Q anomalous-dispersion resonators. Here, we mitigate this confinement-scattering trade-off in pure Ta2O5 waveguides using a fabrication flow based on the Damascene concept. The resulting microring resonators (MRRs) with a cross-section of 1.6 {\mu}m x 0.85 {\mu}m exhibit intrinsic quality factors exceeding 4.0 x 106, corresponding to propagation losses below 10 dB/m, while maintaining anomalous dispersion suitable for bright dissipative Kerr soliton operation. Using these resonators, we generate a coherent bright single-soliton microcomb with a repetition rate of 108.32 GHz. Under optimized dual-pump operating conditions, the platform further exhibits an experimentally accessible single-soliton window spanning 7.5 GHz, indicating a large detuning tolerance for soliton operation; this broad operating window is consistent with the relatively weak thermo-optic response of Ta2O5. Thermal-bistability analysis further indicates that the residual scattering loss is comparable to the material-absorption loss, rather than dominating the loss budget. These results demonstrate that low optical loss, tight mode confinement, and dispersion engineering suitable for soliton formation can be jointly achieved in a pure Ta2O5 platform, providing an ultra-low-loss platform foundation for integrated nonlinear photonic devices and more complex chip-scale nonlinear photonic systems.

title: Resonant dispersive wave emission: a route toward few-cycle, tunable strong-field drivers in the visible
abstract: Intense ultrafast lasers are the backbone of strong-field physics and enable table-top scale applications of coherent high-photon energy radiation through high-harmonic generation (HHG). Using short-wavelength drivers in HHG promises highly efficient conversion into the extreme ultraviolet, but short pulse durations are essential to this approach. We generate multi-GW peak power, sub-10 fs pulses in the visible with broad spectral tunability (220--752 nm) by harnessing soliton dynamics in large-core, gas-filled capillary fibers for high-energy resonant dispersive wave emission. This establishes the potential of resonant dispersive waves as a new class of driving lasers for HHG and strong-field physics in addition to widespread applications in ultrafast spectroscopy.

summaries.en: The paper reports generating multi-GW, sub-10 fs, broadly tunable (220–752 nm) visible pulses by using soliton dynamics in large-core gas-filled capillary fibers to drive resonant dispersive wave emission, establishing resonant dispersive waves as tunable strong-field drivers for efficient high-harmonic generation and ultrafast spectroscopy.
summaries.zh: 论文通过在大芯径充气毛细光纤中利用孤子动力学实现谐振色散波辐射，获得多千兆瓦峰值功率、亚10飞秒且谱宽可调（220–752 nm）的可见光脉冲，从而提出谐振色散波可作为用于高效高次谐波产生与超快光谱的可调强场驱动源。

title: Observation of quadrature-dependent unidirectional flow of light
abstract: Unidirectional transport of light is a central capability in photonics, enabling critical functionalities such as isolation and routing. Ordinarily, this directionality depends on the mode of light, but not its phase. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate phase-dependent unidirectional transport of light for the first time. Specifically, we realize a system where conjugate quadratures of an optical field decouple and propagate in opposite directions. Our all-optical approach uses multiple pump frequencies in a high-$Q$ nanophotonic micro-resonator to achieve Hamiltonian programming through Kerr nonlinearity. Even though we rely on optical nonlinearity, our approach is not limited to any minimal power requirement on the signal. We demonstrate the ultimate limit of this by measuring the effect of quadrature-dependent transport on vacuum fluctuations. Our approach unlocks a fundamental new capability for controlling light, and can enable previously inaccessible regimes of phase-sensitive directional amplification, sensing, and routing.

summaries.en: The paper reports the first experimental demonstration of phase-dependent (quadrature-dependent) unidirectional light transport by using Kerr-driven, Hamiltonian-programmed coupling in a high-Q nanophotonic microresonator so that conjugate field quadratures propagate in opposite directions, including measurements showing the effect on vacuum fluctuations and enabling new regimes of phase-sensitive amplification, sensing, and routing.
summaries.zh: 论文首次实验实现了相位依赖（正交/象限依赖）的单向光传输：通过在高Q纳米光子微谐振器中利用Kerr非线性进行哈密顿量编程，使光场的共轭正交分量解耦并向相反方向传播，并进一步测量了其对真空涨落的影响，从而开辟相位敏感放大、传感与路由的新可达工作区。

title: Dual deconvolution multifocal fluorescence response matrix microscopy for aberration-free high-throughput super-resolution imaging
abstract: Fluorescence response matrix imaging enables separate computational correction of excitation and emission aberrations through dual deconvolution, but single-focus acquisition requires a large number of camera frames, limiting its practical use. Multifocal excitation can accelerate acquisition by recording many illumination positions in parallel, but denser foci also increase inter-focus crosstalk, which can bias the estimated excitation and emission optical transfer functions and degrade aberration correction. Here, we introduce high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging with adaptive multifocal illumination, in which the inter-focus spacing of the multifocal lattice is adjusted according to specimen-dependent crosstalk. A programmable digital micromirror device generates multifocal excitation lattices, and the resulting detector-resolved fluorescence responses are assembled into a two-coordinate fluorescence response matrix. Dual deconvolution separately estimates and corrects the excitation and emission optical transfer functions, and the aberration-corrected matrix is then combined in the spatial-frequency domain to reconstruct the aberration-free image. This strategy reduces the number of required camera frames by approximately three orders of magnitude, allowing response matrices with $\sim 10^6$ illumination positions to be acquired within seconds to a few minutes. The accelerated acquisition preserves the aberration-correction capability of dual deconvolution and achieves an estimated lateral resolution of $\sim$100 nm. Applied to heterogeneous mouse brain and kidney tissue, the method enables high-resolution, depth-resolved volumetric imaging while correcting specimen-dependent aberrations. Together, these results establish adaptive multifocal illumination as a practical route to high-throughput aberration-free fluorescence response matrix imaging.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Applied Physics (physics.app-ph); Biological Physics (physics.bio-ph); Computational Physics (physics.comp-ph); Instrumentation and Detectors (physics.ins-det)

summaries.en: The paper presents an adaptive multifocal fluorescence response matrix microscopy method using programmable DMD illumination and dual deconvolution to separately estimate excitation and emission aberrations while reducing camera frames by ~3 orders of magnitude, enabling acquisition of ~10^6 illumination positions in seconds-to-minutes and achieving ~100 nm lateral resolution for depth-resolved volumetric imaging with specimen-dependent aberration correction.
summaries.zh: 本文提出一种自适应多焦荧光响应矩阵显微成像方法：用可编程DMD产生多焦激发并结合双反卷积分别估计激发与发射像差，从而将所需相机帧数降低约三个数量级，在数秒到数分钟内获取约10^6个照明位置并实现约100 nm的横向分辨率，用于对异质组织进行深度分辨的体积成像并校正与样本相关的像差。

title: Comparative Robustness of Mach-Zehender and Microring Photonic Matrix Multipliers Under Laser RIN and Thermal Drift
abstract: Photonic matrix multipliers can accelerate neural-network inference, but their practical utility depends on how optical weight elements respond to source noise, thermal variation, and calibration error. This paper compares Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) and microring-resonator (MRR) implementations under laser relative-intensity noise (RIN), column-wise thermal/phase drift, and their joint action. Two CIFAR-10 classifiers - a compact four-layer CNN and ResNet-8 - are mapped to matched photonic multiply-accumulate chains using common source-distribution, detection, numerical, and calibration assumptions. Both architectures reproduce the same zero-perturbation baseline for each workload: 79.5% classification accuracy for the Small CNN and 70.0% for ResNet-8. Robustness is then evaluated using separate RIN-only and drift-only sweeps and a full two-dimensional RIN-drift grid, with dimensionless RMS perturbation levels extending from 0.5% to 20%. The analysis reports classification accuracy, class normalized confusion matrices, rolling-accuracy traces, one-dimensional robustness curves, and multidimensional response surfaces. Device equations and parameter definitions follow the models implemented in the QPI Labs Photonic Inference Simulator, with shared laser fluctuations propagated as correlated multiplicative noise and slow drift represented as a per-output-column perturbation of calibrated weights. All numerical results are generated from recorded experiment configurations and random seeds. The study provides a controlled system-level framework for comparing interferometric and resonant photonic weight elements while limiting conclusions to the implemented device models, perturbation ranges, calibration policy, and neural-network workloads.

summaries.en: The paper systematically compares Mach-Zehnder and microring resonator photonic matrix multipliers for two CIFAR-10 CNN/ResNet workloads under laser RIN and thermal/phase drift, using matched simulation assumptions and mapped device models to produce robustness metrics across RIN-only, drift-only, and combined RIN-drift perturbation grids, reporting baseline accuracies of 79.
summaries.zh: 本文在统一的映射与仿真假设下，系统比较了用于CIFAR-10的两类CNN/ResNet工作负载中基于马赫-曾德（MZM）与微环谐振器（MRR）的光子矩阵乘法器在激光相对强度噪声（RIN）与热/相位漂移（含两者联合）作用下的鲁棒性表现，给出基线准确率79.

title: From Microresonator to Packaged Microcomb System: Fiber-Coupled Module and System Integration
abstract: We demonstrate a compact and robust soliton microcomb source designed for field-deployable operation. A directly fiber-coupled SiN microresonator was integrated with precise thermal control into a palm-sized module, reducing the footprint and volume by 16- and 81-fold, respectively. The module, together with the laser sources and optical amplifiers required for microcomb generation, was further integrated into a 19-inch rack-mounted enclosure, achieving system-level footprint and volume reductions of 2.3- and 3.7-fold, respectively. The packaged system achieved a 90% manual startup success rate and maintained continuous soliton operation for 18.8 days, while remaining operational under substantial temperature variations. A state-based automated startup scheme using discrete microcomb-state evaluation achieved single-soliton generation without manual intervention with success rates of 50% within 2 min and 60% within 3 min. Moreover, automated soliton initiation and sustained operation were demonstrated while the packaged microresonator module was directly subjected to random mechanical vibration. These results provide a practical platform for compact, robust, and field-deployable microcomb sources.

summaries.en: The paper presents a compact, fiber-coupled and thermally controlled packaged soliton microcomb system that reduces size and volume at both module and rack levels, achieves high manual and automated startup success, sustains soliton operation under temperature and mechanical vibration variations, and enables field-deployable microcomb generation.
summaries.zh: 论文提出了一种紧凑、直接光纤耦合并集成精确热控的封装型孤子微梳系统，在模块与19英寸机架层面分别大幅缩小体积与占地，并在温度变化及随机机械振动下实现高成功率的手动与自动启动、持续孤子工作，从而为野外可部署的微梳产生提供了可行平台。

title: Tornado Wave-Encoded Point Spread Functions for Multi-Period Three-Dimensional Localization Imaging
abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) localization microscopy using rotational point spread functions (PSFs) is fundamentally challenged by limited axial range, poor PSF compactness, and depth-decoding ambiguity -- particularly in dense specimens with heavy PSF overlap. To address these limitations, we introduce a 3D localization approach based on tornado wave (ToW)-PSFs, combined with a convolutional neural network (CNN) designed to decode continuous rotational patterns and resolve multi-period axial ambiguity. Our engineered PSF encodes the 3D position of each nanoparticle into a compact double-lobe pattern whose orientation rotates with axial position. This design yields a clean, well-defined structural evolution across an unprecedented 15 um axial range, with an average rotation rate of 21.8 degrees/um, ensuring robust long-range depth encoding. To recover coordinates from overlapping emitters, we systematically benchmark a conventional matching-pursuit (MP) algorithm against our CNN. While MP performs adequately in sparse scenes, the CNN demonstrates exceptional robustness in dense fields, achieving a 70.24% localization accuracy at 20 particles per image-substantially outperforming MP's 22.52% -- while also significantly suppressing axial period-jump errors. Experimental validation on nanoparticles confirms reliable single- and multi-particle localization throughout the entire working range. Our results establish ToW-PSFs as a powerful and practical optical encoding strategy for high-density, extended-range 3D localization imaging.

summaries.en: The paper presents tornado wave–encoded point spread functions combined with a CNN to enable robust long-range, high-density 3D localization microscopy by compactly encoding axial position into a rotating double-lobe PSF pattern and resolving multi-period depth ambiguities, outperforming matching pursuit especially in dense scenes.
summaries.zh: 本文提出将龙卷波编码点扩散函数（ToW-PSFs）与卷积神经网络结合，用紧凑的旋转双叶PSF结构对轴向位置进行编码并消除多周期深度歧义，从而实现长工作距离的高密度3D定位成像，并在密集场景下显著优于匹配追踪算法。

title: Direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire for wide-band photonics
abstract: Low-loss stoichiometric silicon nitride on oxidized silicon has emerged as the major wide-band photonics platform for nonlinear and quantum photonics. These films, deposited by low-pressure chemical vapor deposition (LPCVD), are well known to have around 1000 MPa of residual tensile stress, which often leads to cracking when film thickness exceeds 400 nm. Although various stress-mitigation approaches can isolate or prevent cracking, this stress issue remains a major fabrication challenge. Low-residual-stress LPCVD stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire has also been reported and recently explored for photonics at telecommunication wavelengths. Here, we advance its development through systematic characterization, including thin-film stress analysis, ellipsometry and prism-coupling measurements of refractive index and loss, and swept-wavelength spectroscopy of fabricated photonic devices across a broad range of wavelengths. We demonstrate the direct growth of crack-free stoichiometric silicon nitride up to 2 {\mu}m thick with only 200 MPa of stress. Our fabricated devices show propagation losses of 0.35 dB/cm around 780 nm, 0.37 dB/cm around 1064 nm, and 0.25 dB/cm around 1630 nm. In addition, prism-coupling measurements indicate film losses below 1 dB/cm at wavelengths down to 500 nm. Our work highlights stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire as a promising wide-band photonics platform.

summaries.en: The paper characterizes and advances low-residual-stress LPCVD stoichiometric silicon nitride on sapphire, demonstrating direct crack-free growth up to 2 μm thickness with 200 MPa stress and reporting low optical propagation losses across 500–1630 nm for wide-band photonics relevant to nonlinear and quantum photonics.
summaries.zh: 论文通过系统表征并推进低残余应力的LPCVD化学气相沉积配方，在蓝宝石上实现高质量无裂纹的化学计量硅氮薄膜：厚度可达2 μm且仅有200 MPa应力，并在500–1630 nm范围内获得低光传播损耗，表明其作为面向非线性与量子光子学的宽带光子学平台具有潜力。

title: Photon-efficient readout of optical cavity arrays via spatial heterodyne
abstract: Optical cavity arrays are an emerging tool for efficiently interfacing optical photons to quantum emitters for applications such as quantum computing. In this work, we demonstrate a metrology technique for such cavity arrays by interfering cavity array outputs against a tilted reference beam on a camera, constituting a spatial heterodyne. Both the amplitude and phase of each cavity's transmitted field can be extracted from the resulting images. Enabled by the improved scaling of heterodyne detection over intensity detection in the presence of technical noise, we demonstrate signal-to-noise ratio greater than one down to the single detected photon level, even in the presence of hundreds of noise equivalent photons. This readout technique holds promise for fast, non-destructive imaging of atomic qubits in cavity arrays by requiring fewer scattered photons while allowing the use of fast cameras with higher electronic readout noise.

summaries.en: The paper presents a spatial heterodyne metrology method that interferes optical cavity-array outputs with a tilted reference beam on a camera to extract each cavity’s transmitted-field amplitude and phase, achieving photon-efficient readout with signal-to-noise above one at the single-photon level despite substantial technical noise, enabling fast, non-destructive imaging of atomic qubits with fewer scattered photons.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种空间非零差（spatial heterodyne）测量方法：将光学腔阵列的输出与倾斜参考光束在相机上干涉，从而从图像中提取每个腔透射场的振幅与相位，并利用与强度测量相比在技术噪声存在下更好的异频检测标度实现高达单光子探测水平仍信噪比大于1，即使存在数百个噪声等效光子，该方法有望以更少散射光子实现对腔阵列中原子比特的快速、非破坏性成像。

title: Transfer learning-aided, artificial intelligence approach to evaluate optical properties of materials for classical and quantum photonic applications
abstract: In this study, an artificial intelligence-assisted evaluation of the refractive indices of different materials is performed. The evaluation of the refractive index is necessary to design photonic devices for various classical and quantum photonic applications, and to theoretically analyse experimental results. The refractive index is one of the crucial parameters that affect the interaction of light with matter. Although the refractive index can be measured experimentally, its estimation via computational means provide the advantage of not requiring costly instrumentation, trained researchers and could avoid potential laboratory-based uncertainties. Therefore, in this study, artificial intelligence is implemented to estimate the optical constants of two types of materials, i.e., noble metals, and semiconductors. To this end, an artificial neural network is used to estimate the real and the imaginary parts of the refractive index of a specific material for various wavelengths of light. Then, the knowledge of the trained neural network is employed to initiate and train new neural networks to estimate the refractive indices of other materials. For the training of a neural network, various methods can be deployed. However, the application of the training can be a time-consuming process. A transfer learning approach is here implemented to provide a faster training solution for the problem under study. The implementation of transfer learning allows training the neural networks for a new material with higher speed or accuracy when compared to non-knowledge transfer-based training. Our results show the efficiency of the proposed technique in accurately evaluating the real and imaginary parts of the refractive index of different materials.

summaries.en: The paper presents a transfer-learning–aided artificial neural network approach to rapidly and accurately estimate the real and imaginary refractive indices of noble metals and semiconductors across wavelengths for classical and quantum photonic device design and analysis.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出了一种结合迁移学习的人工神经网络方法，可在不同波长范围内快速且准确估计贵金属与半导体的实部与虚部折射率，用于经典与量子光子器件设计及实验结果分析。

title: Programmable spatiotemporal shaping for partially coherent structured wave packets
abstract: Providing more coherent light with space-time coupling offers unprecedented opportunities across diverse scientific disciplines and areas of technology. However, in many applications, tailored laser beams with partial coherence in space and time are desired. Here, we demonstrate a programmable approach for simultaneously shaping the intensity and coherence distributions of spatiotemporally coupled partially coherent wave packets. By jointly engineering the fractal speckle of a dynamic scatterer and applying tailored modulation of the illumination function, we experimentally generate partially coherent laser beams with arbitrarily designed intensity and nontrivial coherence distributions. The proposed approach is compatible with ultrafast laser pulses, enabling the on-demand generation of partially coherent space-time wave packets. The resulting spatiotemporally partially coherent wave packets exhibit non-separable space-time intensity profiles together with engineered spatiotemporal correlation distributions. This work provides a versatile framework for tailoring partially coherent light in space and time, with varied applications in relativistic laser-matter interaction, passive imaging and optical manipulation.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates a programmable method to simultaneously shape the intensity and spatiotemporal coherence of partially coherent, spatiotemporally coupled wave packets by engineering the fractal speckle of a dynamic scatterer and applying tailored illumination modulation, producing ultrafast-capable beams with arbitrarily designed intensity and nontrivial correlation distributions and non-separable space-time structure for applications in laser-matter interaction, imaging, and optical manipulation.

title: High Sensitivity Transient Holographic Full-Polarization Microscopy
abstract: The polarization state of light provides direct access to ultrafast electronic, magnetic, and structural dynamics in materials. Transient wide-field microscopy with simultaneous amplitude, phase, and polarization sensitivity enables spatially resolved measurements of these dynamics, but its sensitivity is often limited by technical noise and background fluctuations. Here, we demonstrate transient holographic full-polarization microscopy with substantially reduced instrumental noise and sensitivity approaching the shot-noise limit. We compare holographic geometries using one, two, and four reference beams and find that the single-reference configuration provides the most favourable shot-noise-limited sensitivity for the derived polarization observables. Combined with two-camera detection, it simultaneously captures both orthogonal polarization components without distributing reference photons among multiple carriers. A self-referenced noise-reduction framework combining singular value decomposition and background subtraction further suppresses correlated noise. For spatially averaged regions, the baseline noise is reduced by factors of three-sixty, enabling detection of weaker transient responses at lower excitation densities and in weakly absorbing materials.

summaries.en: The paper presents transient holographic full-polarization wide-field microscopy with greatly reduced instrumental noise, near shot-noise-limited sensitivity, an optimized single-reference-beam geometry for polarization observables, dual-camera capture of orthogonal polarization components, and a self-referenced SVD/background-noise-reduction framework that lowers baseline noise by up to 360× to detect weaker ultrafast transient responses at lower excitation densities.

title: Fading Memory and Nonlinear Dynamics in a Microring Resonator Network and their Use in Computation
abstract: Silicon microring resonators are promising components for photonic reservoir computing because their nonlinear optical response can transform signals and retain information about recent inputs. Under constant optical excitation, their coupled free-carrier and thermal dynamics can generate self-pulsing: a periodic output response. However, constant-input behavior does not reveal how these dynamics respond to randomly modulated signals or whether their memory is useful for temporal processing. Here, we characterize a single silicon microring resonator and a passive network of microring resonators under random input modulation. The temporal component associated with self-pulsing remains observable under random modulation, but the largest fading memory occurs near the self-pulsing boundary, where no resolved self-pulsing-like oscillation is present. reservoir computing metrics, such as memory capacity, map this accessible memory, and its decay provides effective timescales associated mainly with free-carrier and thermal relaxation. Finally, we use NARMA reconstruction to test whether the measured memory profile supports nonlinear temporal processing. Responses with a resolved self-pulsing-like component perform worse on this task, and the intrinsic memory profile is not matched to the required input history. These results show that reservoir computing metrics can characterize nonlinear microring resonator dynamics even when the physical system is not an effective standalone reservoir for the selected task.

summaries.en: The paper characterizes how free-carrier/thermal dynamics in silicon microring resonator (networks) under random modulation preserve self-pulsing-related fading memory near the self-pulsing boundary, uses reservoir-computing metrics to extract relevant relaxation timescales, and finds that while these metrics can quantify nonlinear dynamics, the intrinsic memory profile and especially resolved self-pulsing-like behavior do not support NARMA temporal nonlinear processing for the tested task.
summaries.zh: 本文表征了在随机调制输入下，硅微环谐振器（及其网络）中由自由载流子/热效应驱动的动态如何在接近自脉冲边界时保留与自脉冲相关的衰减记忆，利用储备计算指标提取主要由自由载流子与热弛豫决定的有效时间尺度，并通过NARMA重建发现尽管这些指标能刻画非线性动态，但系统的内在记忆特性（尤其是出现可分辨自脉冲成分时）并不匹配所测试任务所需的输入历史，因而难以有效完成该非线性时间处理。

title: Asynchronous Terahertz-field sampling with soliton microcombs
abstract: Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy records the electric field of terahertz transients and underpins applications from materials science to non-destructive testing. Asynchronous optical sampling enables systems without moving parts, but its acquisition rate remains fundamentally limited by the repetition-rate of the driving femtosecond lasers. Here, we demonstrate asynchronous terahertz-field sampling with two chip-based soliton microcombs. Their ultrahigh 25 GHz pulse repetition-rate drastically reduces dead-time during acquisition, and stabilization via sideband injection-locking enables coherent averaging without active feedback loops. At 10 kHz acquisition rate, we achieve a dynamic range of 74 dB in a single 100 $\mu$s scan, and 100 dB after 50 ms of coherent averaging with a 1.6 THz bandwidth. Acquisition rates of up to 100 kHz are demonstrated, limited only by detection electronics. Together with a proof-of-concept silicon wafer thickness measurement, these results establish soliton microcombs as compact sources for rapid terahertz-field sampling.

title: Image Priors for Single-Shot Coded Diffraction Phase Retrieval
abstract: Phase retrieval recovers complex-valued objects from intensity-only measurements. In its classical Fourier form, reconstruction suffers from twin-image stagnation. Coded diffraction imaging, which adds a random phase mask before the Fourier transform, has so far required several masks. We show that an image prior makes single-shot coded diffraction imaging possible, with a single random mask followed by a Fourier transform. We validate this claim in simulation and in an optical experiment, in which a spatial light modulator displays the phase object together with the random mask. Our experimental validation covers five test signals and 530 images from the public Brno quantitative phase microscopy dataset of five adherent cell lines. With no image prior or with Fourier-only measurements, reconstruction of complex-valued objects from a single diffraction pattern consistently fails. An out-of-the-box pretrained image denoiser enables accurate reconstruction, in simulation even with fewer measurements than unknowns. Five regularization frameworks built on the same denoiser and one learned weakly convex regularizer all reconstruct the experimental images with peak signal-to-noise ratios within one decibel of each other. A single random phase mask and image priors thus turn coded diffraction imaging into a practical single-shot modality for quantitative phase imaging.

summaries.en: The paper shows that by combining an image prior with a single random phase mask in coded diffraction phase retrieval, complex-valued optical objects can be accurately reconstructed from a single intensity diffraction pattern, validated by simulations and an SLM-based optical experiment using 530 microscopy images, while reconstructions without priors or Fourier-only measurements fail and multiple denoiser-based regularizers achieve similar high-quality results.
summaries.zh: 本文表明，将图像先验与单个随机相位掩模结合，可在仅凭一个强度衍射图样的情况下实现对复杂光学对象的准确相位重建；作者通过仿真和使用空间光调制器的光学实验验证了该方法，并在基于布尔诺定量相位显微镜公开数据集的530幅细胞图像上测试，结果显示不使用先验或仅用傅里叶测量时重建会失败，而多种基于同一去噪器的正则化框架均能获得彼此接近的高质量结果。

title: Chiral Vector Beams for Topological Enantio-Sensitive Imaging
abstract: Molecular chiral discrimination is vital across chemistry and life sciences, yet optical approaches remain highly inefficient for small organic molecules. Here we turn vector beams, whose polarization carries a topological charge, into an efficient probe of molecular handedness. We show that the combination of a tightly focused radially polarized beam at the fundamental frequency {\omega} and an azimuthally polarized beam at 2{\omega} creates chiral vector beams, a locally chiral field with structured handedness. Using state-of-the-art computational modeling in the chiral molecule carvone, we show that the nonlinear response (notably sum-frequency generation) of randomly oriented chiral molecules to this chiral vector beam captures the fields' local handedness and is highly enantio-sensitive. The two enantiomers emit light at frequency 3{\omega} with topological ring structures of different divergence, and thus the molecular handedness can be read out directly from the ring radius. The signal inherits the Poincaré index of the driving field, opening up new ways to robust, ultrafast, and and all-optical chiral discrimination.

summaries.en: The paper proposes using chiral vector beams—generated by combining a tightly focused radially polarized beam at ω with an azimuthally polarized beam at 2ω—to drive enantio-sensitive nonlinear (sum-frequency) imaging of small chiral molecules, where different enantiomers produce 3ω emission with topological ring structures whose ring radius reveals molecular handedness and whose signal inherits the Poincaré index of the driving field.
summaries.zh: 论文提出通过将ω处的紧聚焦径向偏振光与2ω处的方位偏振光结合来产生手性矢量光束，并利用其驱动小型手性分子的非线性（和频）响应实现高灵敏的对映体成像：不同对映体在3ω处发射出发散度不同的拓扑环结构，环半径可直接读出分子手性，且信号继承驱动场的庞加莱指数。

title: Observation of Photon Bunching in Broadband Multimode Thermal Light Enabled by Temporal Imaging
abstract: Photons emitted by incoherent sources exhibit temporal bunching, a fundamental manifestation of Bose-Einstein statistics first observed by Hanbury Brown and Twiss (HBT). While intensity correlation measurements originated in astronomy and are now central across quantum technologies, biophysics, and spectroscopy, observing temporal bunching in broadband thermal light remains limited by detector temporal resolution. Conventional approaches - such as streak cameras or optical upconversion - introduce severe trade-offs in efficiency, bandwidth, or setup versatility. Here, we propose and demonstrate a third route: pre-detection temporal magnification of the optical field prior to measuring its intensity autocorrelation function in a conventional HBT setup. Using an electro-optic time lens with a temporal magnification of 660, we resolve the temporal intensity autocorrelation of broadband thermal light generated via non-degenerate spontaneous parametric down-conversion with a bandwidth of 250 GHz. This enables direct observation of thermal photon bunching on sub-3.5 picosecond timescales without narrow spectral filtering, establishing pre-detection temporal imaging as a general platform for broadband statistical optics, with applications spanning ultrafast quantum optics, biophysical imaging, and potentially stellar intensity interferometry.

title: Practical Mid-infrared Dual-comb Spectroscopy with Absolute Frequency Referencing Based on a Single-cavity Dual-comb Fiber Laser
abstract: We demonstrate a practical mid-infrared (MIR) dual-comb spectroscopy (DCS) method based on a bidirectional dual-comb fiber laser. By exploiting the inherently high relative stability and mutual coherence of the dual-comb laser, we stabilize the MIR dual-comb modes with sufficient precision using only piezoelectric control of the repetition frequencies. This simple configuration enables correction of residual timing jitter and phase noise in interferograms while preserving the absolute optical frequency scale defined by the experimentally obtained comb parameters, without requiring an external continuous-wave laser reference or tight phase-locking. Importantly, the proposed method does not merely produce apparently clean interferograms through signal processing, but enables coherent averaging while retaining both the physically meaningful interferometric waveforms and well-defined absolute frequency information. The proposed system is experimentally validated through MIR spectroscopy of N$_2$O around 3.9 $\mu$m, achieving a signal-to-noise ratio of approximately 690 through coherent averaging of 10,000 interferograms over 65 s, along with the acquisition of an absorption spectrum consistent with the reference data. These results demonstrate a simple and practical approach to absolute-frequency-referenced MIR-DCS.

summaries.en: The paper presents a simple, absolute-frequency-referenced mid-infrared dual-comb spectroscopy system using a bidirectional single-cavity dual-comb fiber laser that stabilizes dual-comb modes with piezo-controlled repetition frequencies, enabling coherent averaging with correct timing-jitter/phase-noise behavior without an external CW reference, and demonstrates N2O spectroscopy near 3.

title: On-chip optical isolators
abstract: Optical isolation suppresses back-reflections that destabilize lasers, produce parasitic interference, and increase crosstalk in photonic systems. Although free-space and fibre-optic isolators are mature, no broadly adopted on-chip technology yet combines strong isolation, low insertion loss, broad bandwidth, compact footprint, and scalable fabrication. The difficulty is twofold: Lorentz reciprocity must be broken, and every relevant backward spatial, spectral, and polarization channel must be suppressed. This Review develops a common framework for assessing proposed solutions. We first distinguish pairwise nonreciprocity from intensity-asymmetric transmission and from true isolation using the constitutive relations and scattering matrix. We then compare three physical routes to an integrated nonreciprocal response: magneto-optical bias, externally driven space-time modulation, and nonlinear optical processes. Topological and non-Hermitian systems are treated as cross-cutting design frameworks that can route, protect, or enhance an underlying nonreciprocal response, but do not by themselves break reciprocity. Finally, we examine fundamental constraints and practical trade-offs among isolation, insertion loss, bandwidth, footprint, modal coverage, drive requirements, and fabrication compatibility. The resulting mechanism-based perspective connects reciprocity-breaking physics to the requirements of scalable photonic integrated circuits.
subjects: Optics (physics.optics) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall); Materials Science (cond-mat.mtrl-sci)

summaries.en: This Review proposes a unified framework to assess on-chip optical isolators, clarifying how true nonreciprocity differs from asymmetric transmission, comparing magneto-optical bias, space-time modulation, and nonlinear effects as routes to isolation, and outlining key constraints and trade-offs for achieving strong, broad-band, low-loss, scalable on-chip performance.
summaries.zh: 本综述提出用于评估片上光学隔离器的统一框架，阐明真正的非互易性与非对称透射的区别，比较采用磁光偏置、时空调制与非线性效应的隔离实现路径，并总结实现强隔离、宽带、低损耗且可扩展片上性能的关键约束与权衡。

title: A Photonic Integrated Light Generation, Control, and Delivery Engine for Creating Cold Atoms
abstract: The creation of cold atoms underpins quantum sensing and precision metrology, computing, timekeeping, and fundamental science experiments. Miniaturizing the lasers and optical infrastructure, which occupy over 80% of the volume of these experiments, through photonic integration could improve robustness, reliability, and manufacturability while reducing cost and enabling portable space-based precision measurements and quantum tools for non-experts. Yet, there has been limited progress towards integration of the laser and optical infrastructure required to generate cold atoms onto a single chip. We demonstrate a photonic engine that generates, controls, and delivers precision light to create cold atoms in a rubidium 3-dimensional magneto-optical trap (3D-MOT). We integrate on a single chip two frequency-agile self-injection-locked lasers, laser frequency and intensity control, passive beam combining and splitting, signal monitoring, and high-efficiency beam delivery to a rubidium vapor cell. The integrated engine is shown to support multiple functions required for generating cold atoms including stable generation of low-noise cooling and repump light, frequency control for atom spectroscopy and stabilization, real-time laser monitoring, routing for laser offset locking, optical power modulation, and large-area three-beam delivery of 3 mW to the physics package. Fully electrically controlled, the engine enables sustained 3D-MOT operation, trapping more than 1 million atoms at an average temperature of 350 uK and supporting atom-number and temperature measurements. These results demonstrate the first single-chip integration of light generation, control, and delivery for cold-atom generation, offering a path toward smaller, more robust, and manufacturable cold-atom systems for applications including cold-atom clocks and sensors.

summaries.en: The paper reports a fully electrically controlled single-chip photonic integrated “engine” that generates, frequency- and intensity-controls, monitors, and efficiently delivers low-noise cooling and repump beams to a rubidium 3D magneto-optical trap, enabling sustained trapping of over one million atoms at 350 µK with support for spectroscopy and temperature/atom-number measurements.
summaries.zh: 该论文提出并实现了一个全电控的单芯片光子集成“引擎”，可在鲁本纳三维磁光阱中生成、进行频率与强度控制、监测并高效输送低噪声冷却与回泵光束，从而实现持续工作并俘获超过100万原子且平均温度为350 µK，同时支持原子谱学以及原子数与温度测量。

title: Recovery-Oriented Optical System Design Based on Fisher Information
abstract: Traditional optical system design for imaging applications has long been guided by image quality metrics such as geometrical RMS spot size, wavefront error, and modulation transfer function (MTF). Although these metrics effectively characterize direct imaging performance, they do not necessarily indicate optimal behavior when image restoration is subsequently applied. In modern imaging pipelines, however, optical systems are increasingly combined with physics-based or learning-based restoration methods, making the information transfer properties of the optical system critically important. In this work, we propose a recovery-oriented optical design approach that explicitly links optical system optimization with image restoration performance through an estimation-theoretic framework based on Fisher information. A new design criterion is adopted to ensure that the information encoded by the optical system can be reliably recovered during image restoration. To validate the proposed approach, two dual separated aspheric lenses are designed under identical configurations using conventional RMS-based optimization and the proposed recovery-oriented optimization, respectively. Although the RMS-optimized lens exhibits superior direct imaging quality, it underperforms after image restoration compared to the recovery-oriented design. These results demonstrate that recovery-oriented optical design provides a physically interpretable and effective extension of traditional optical design criteria for imaging systems operating within modern computational imaging pipelines.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a recovery-oriented optical system design framework using Fisher information to optimize optics for reliable image restoration, showing that lenses optimized by conventional RMS metrics can yield worse restored results than those optimized for recovery-based information transfer.

title: Imaging the building blocks of ant pheromone communication
abstract: Organisms have evolved diverse strategies to communicate. Beyond acoustic and visual signals, many species rely on chemical communication, including pheromones: volatile compounds involved in reproduction, defense, and coordination. Ant trail systems, a paradigm of pheromone use, have inspired decades of research in collective behavior, self-organization and optimization algorithms. Yet, despite their central role, individual pheromone deposits have never been directly visualized or quantified, limiting our understanding of how deposition events scale into collective trail formation. Here, we use interferometric imaging to reveal and quantify single pheromone deposits in the ant Lasius niger. This label-free, non-invasive approach enables precise measurement of single deposit volume (~1 pL, with x20-fold variability), morphology, and temporal dynamics. We uncover a two-phase volume loss process: most of secreted volume evaporates within seconds, forming a dried droplet, which then partially sublimates (~10%) over one hour. These findings challenge the assumption of homogeneous deposition and bring previously inaccessible properties of ant pheromone trails within experimental reach. Our method establishes a quantitative framework for studying the spatiotemporal dynamics of insect chemical communication, linking individual signaling to collective patterns.

summaries.en: The paper uses interferometric, label-free imaging to visualize and quantify single pheromone deposits of the ant Lasius niger, revealing ~1 pL deposits with large variability and a two-phase post-deposition loss where most volume evaporates within seconds and about 10% sublimates over an hour, enabling quantitative study of how individual chemical signaling scales to collective trail formation.

title: Chirality Inversion and Giant Optical Activity in Scalable Self-Assembled Metamaterials
abstract: Chiral materials manipulate light in ways that hold promise for sensing, imaging, and photonics, but producing such materials with strong and reproducible optical activity at large scale remains challenging. Here, we develop a scalable strategy to assemble hierarchical helicoidal metamaterials from metallic nanoparticles and chitin nanocrystals, a biosourced polysaccharide. Spontaneous co-assembly produces ordered chiral structures with strong plasmonic optical activity, reaching a dissymmetry factor of 0.55. The unprecedented ability to vary the helicoidal pitch allows control of the optical response, enabling inversion of optical handedness without changing the handedness of the template, effectively decoupling geometrical chirality from optical chirality. Remarkably, the gold nanoparticles can also be recovered from dry films and redispersed as colloids, introducing an appealing circularity concept for sustainable chiral plasmonic materials.

title: Experimental Demonstration of 7-Dimensional N-Vector Model with Dimensional Inflation and Annealing
abstract: We report the first experimental realization of a physical system described by a high-dimensional Hamiltonian comprising up to seven dimensions. Our setup is based on a holographic optical computer, which realizes a dimensional inflation by spatial and temporal multiplexing of lower dimensional systems. We demonstrate an $N$-vector model, with applications in field theory and computing. The approach is scalable and enables table-top implementation of high-dimensional theoretical models, and novel methods for combinatorial optimization. We experimentally demonstrate dimensional annealing: by dynamically reducing the number of dimensions, the ground state of an Ising model is found in complex graphs by an adiabatic evolution from high-dimensional spaces.

summaries.en: The paper presents the first experimental realization of a up to seven-dimensional Hamiltonian using a holographic optical computer that performs dimensional inflation via spatial and temporal multiplexing, demonstrates a scalable N-vector model for computing and combinatorial optimization, and experimentally verifies dimensional annealing by reducing dimensions during adiabatic evolution to obtain Ising ground states on complex graphs.

title: Feedback-Controlled Self-Trapping of Solitons
abstract: Chip-scale microresonator-based frequency combs, commonly referred to as microcombs, are promising sources for field-deployable metrology applications. However, intrinsic microresonator noise can make it difficult to generate microcombs with sufficiently low noise for applications. A widely used approach to overcome this limitation is to trap the DKS in the microresonator by phase-modulating the pump laser, although integrating a low-noise modulation reference in a fully on-chip platform remains challenging. Here, we propose an optoelectronic self-trapping scheme in which the impact of intrinsic microresonator noise on microcomb repetition-rate jitter is suppressed through feedback-controlled phase modulation of the driving laser so that the intrinsic noise of the laser sets the ultimate performance limit. This modification eliminates the need for an external low-phase-noise RF source, thereby enabling chip integration. We develop both analytical and numerical models for the proposed system and benchmark its performance against conventional externally referenced bulk implementations, showing that the proposed approach achieves comparable microcomb noise suppression while maintaining chip-scale compatibility.

summaries.en: The paper proposes an optoelectronic self-trapping feedback scheme that phase-modulates the driving laser based on microresonator behavior to suppress intrinsic resonator noise in microcomb repetition-rate jitter, achieving performance comparable to externally referenced bulk systems without requiring an external low-phase-noise RF reference and enabling fully chip-scale integration.
summaries.zh: 论文提出了一种基于反馈的光电自俘获方案，通过对驱动激光实施受控相位调制来抑制微腔固有噪声对微梳重复率抖动的影响，使性能可与外部参考的体器件实现相当，同时无需外部低相噪RF源并实现全芯片尺度集成。

title: Optical parametric amplification of spatiotemporal optical vortices
abstract: Spatiotemporal optical vortices (STOVs) are structured light featuring a phase singularity in the spatiotemporal domain, exhibiting unique topology that couples spatial and temporal dimensions. To date, amplification of STOVs remains unexplored, and their wavelength tunability is limited by available light sources. In this work, we present the theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration of optical parametric amplification (OPA) of STOVs. The pulse energy of the STOV signal is enhanced by a factor of 60, while its spatiotemporal structure is robustly preserved. The generated idler inherits the phase-conjugated STOV topology with the opposite topological charge, governed by simultaneous conservation of energy, linear momentum, and spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum. The intrinsic wavelength-conversion capability of OPA further provides a route towards spectrally tunable STOV generation, spanning from visible to near-infrared wavelength regimes. This work paves the way toward further development of multi-stage amplification architectures, facilitating applications of wavelength-tunable spatiotemporally structured light at ultrahigh intensities.

summaries.en: The paper theoretically analyzes and experimentally demonstrates optical parametric amplification of spatiotemporal optical vortices, achieving a 60× increase in signal pulse energy while preserving the STOV structure, generating an idler with phase-conjugated opposite topological charge via conservation of energy, linear momentum, and spatiotemporal orbital angular momentum, and enabling spectrally tunable STOVs from visible to near-infrared wavelengths for high-intensity, wavelength-adjustable structured-light applications.
summaries.zh: 论文对时空光涡（STOV）的光参量放大进行理论分析与实验验证：将信号脉冲能量提高60倍且稳健保持STOV结构，产生拓扑电荷相反的相位共轭孪生涡（idler），其形成由能量、线动量及时空轨道角动量的同时守恒决定，并利用OPA的内禀波长转换能力实现从可见到近红外的光谱可调STOV生成，为多级放大与高强度波长可调结构光应用奠定基础。

title: Continuous-wave 148.4 nm Generation in Quasi-phase Matched BaMgF4
abstract: We report continuous-wave (CW) vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) generation at 148.4 nm by second-harmonic generation of 296.8-nm fundamental light in quasi-phase matched (QPM) BaMgF4 (BMF). At the incident power of 170 mW, a VUV output power of approximately 31 pW can be obtained. The quadratic dependence of the signal on the incident power in the QPM region and its attenuation in the ambient environment support the identification of VUV generation. The polarization dependence shows a sine-function shape with a 15% output attenuation from the maximum to the minimum. These results highlight the potential of BMF as a nonlinear medium for CW VUV generation.

title: Mode locking by phase-sensitive amplification
abstract: Mode locking is the mechanism by which lasers organize many optical modes into stable trains of ultrashort pulses. It underpins optical frequency combs, precision timing and spectroscopy, and provides the phase-coherent waveforms required for applications ranging from strong-field physics to optical frequency metrology. Conventional pulse-forming mechanisms select pulse amplitude without fixing its phase relative to an external optical reference, leaving pulse formation and optical-phase stabilization as separate functions. Phase-sensitive amplification offers a different possibility: the optical reference can participate directly in pulse formation. Here we demonstrate this principle in a continuously pumped oscillator. Kerr-induced phase evolution and cavity detuning turn pump-referenced parametric gain into a power-dependent discriminator that supports stable single-soliton operation. Roundtrip-resolved interferometry reveals that the soliton optical phase remains referenced to the master laser modulo $\pi$. These results establish phase-sensitive mode locking, in which pulse-amplitude selection and optical-phase referencing arise from the same coherent nonlinear feedback.

summaries.en: The paper demonstrates phase-sensitive mode locking in a continuously pumped oscillator, where Kerr-induced phase evolution and cavity detuning convert pump-referenced parametric gain into a power-dependent discriminator that stabilizes a single-soliton while maintaining the soliton’s optical phase referenced to the master laser modulo π.
summaries.zh: 论文在连续抽运振荡器中实现了相位敏感的模锁定，通过克尔效应引起的相位演化与腔失谐把以泵为参考的参数增益转化为功率相关的判别器，从而稳定单孤子并使孤子的光学相位相对于主激光保持模π的参考关系。

title: Probing topological edge states in multilayer dielectric photonic nanostructures
abstract: Topological photonics has recently attracted a significant attention, leading to many theoretical studies and predictions. However, direct experimental demonstrations of topology-driven effects, particularly in nanostructures, are rarely proven. In this work, we experimentally investigate multilayer photonic nanostructures composed of alternating subwavelength dielectric layers, arranged according to the topological Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By engineering different edge truncations, we probe different supported topological phases. Our theoretical predictions and experimental measurements reveal strong field confinement at the surface exclusively in the configuration supporting topological edge states, providing their localized character and topological origin. First, we demonstrate enhanced absorption in an ultrathin absorbing overlayer deposited on the surface when the topological surface mode is present, highlighting the potential for surface-sensing applications. Second, we observe enhanced second-harmonic generation in reflection from the surface, demonstrating the potential of topological states for surface enhanced nonlinear optics enabled by the strong localization of the electromagnetic field at the interface.

summaries.en: The paper reports experiments on multilayer dielectric photonic nanostructures implementing the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger topological model, showing that specific edge truncations support topological edge states with exclusive surface field confinement that enables enhanced surface absorption and topologically enhanced nonlinear (second-harmonic) generation.
summaries.zh: 论文通过实现 Su-Schrieffer-Heeger 拓扑模型的多层介质光子纳米结构实验表明，特定的边缘截断仅在支持拓扑边态时才会出现表面独有的强场局域性，并据此实现增强的表面吸收与由界面强局域电磁场驱动的拓扑增强二次谐波反射。

title: Progress in Cavitated Front Gridline Ag Paste for PERC Solar Cell Architecture
abstract: This paper reports on the progress made with the cavitated silver paste on passivated emitter rear contact cells (PERC) to reduce the series resistance. Thus, electrical and microscopy characterizations are used to examine these resistive losses. Fifteen 252 cm2 PERC cells were fabricated for this assessment. Under standard test conditions, these cells achieved a mean conversion efficiency of 21.87% and a maximum of 22.07%. The mean measured fill factor was 79.98%, compared with a pseudo-fill factor of 83.60%, giving a mean deficit of 3.62 percentage points. Fill factor decreased with increasing area-normalized series resistance, which ranged from 0.53 to 0.83 ohm-cm2, while open-circuit voltage and short-circuit current remained unvaried. These electrical trends support resistive current extraction as the principal contributor to fill-factor variation. Electroluminescence imaging revealed localized emission nonuniformity. Cross-sectional scanning transmission electron microscopy showed variation in the glass interfacial layer, while scanning electron microscopy identified micrometer and sub micrometer silver particles. Conductive atomic force microscopy after sequential removal of the bulk metal and glass revealed spatially heterogeneous current response. These observations are consistent with nonuniform electrical access at the contact, where restricted conducting pathways may concentrate on current and increase local voltage drops. The combined characterization identifies interfacial heterogeneity and the connectivity of conducting pathways as priorities for understanding and reducing extraction losses in cavitated silver metallization.

summaries.zh: 本文评估了用于PERC太阳能电池的空腔银浆以降低串联电阻，结果显示平均效率达21.

title: Predictive Holonomy and Minimal Completion of Coarse Dynamics
abstract: A coarse description of a dynamical system generally fails to evolve autonomously: evolving and coarse-graining in different orders gives different predictions, and the compressed propagator fails the semigroup law. We show that this path dependence is the observable boundary of missing state. For a finite continuous-time Markov chain with generator $L$, coarse channel $C$, and stochastic section $R$ satisfying $CR=I$, define $P=RC$, $Q=I-P$, and $K=CLR$. The exact coarse propagator $T_t=C\mathrm{e}^{tL}R$ obeys a Volterra equation with memory kernel $\mathcal{M}(t)=CLQ\,\mathrm{e}^{tQLQ}\,QLR$. Every memory jet $\mathcal{M}^{(k)}(0)$ is recursively recoverable from the short-time derivatives of $T_t$ alone. The rank of the block Hankel operator $\mathbb{H}_{\infty}=(\mathcal{M}^{(i+j)}(0))_{i,j\geq 0}$ is exactly the smallest number of auxiliary linear state variables required to turn the coarse dynamics into an exact autonomous, time-homogeneous system. A minimal completion is constructible by Ho--Kalman factorization and is unique up to similarity. If $d=\min\{k:\mathcal{M}^{(k)}(0)\neq 0\}$, then every smooth classical $f$-divergence generically scales as $t^{2d+4}$. Exact Markov examples realize exponents $4,6,8$ and closure ranks $1,2,3$. We also derive finite-sample singular-value certificates for hidden predictive coordinates, including a matrix-Bernstein bound with intrinsic-variance control. Finally, histories are identified when they induce the same future law under every admissible intervention, yielding the minimal counterfactual predictive state. The results turn coarse-graining into a constructive state-completion problem and separate ordinary linear realization from the harder requirement of a positive or Markov realization.

summaries.en: The paper shows that path dependence in coarse-grained dynamics corresponds to missing state information and provides a minimal, constructive completion—characterized by the rank of a Hankel operator and recoverable memory jets—turning coarse evolution into an exact autonomous Markov-like system while yielding generic power-law scaling for divergences and finite-sample certificates for hidden predictive coordinates.
summaries.zh: 论文证明粗粒化动力学中的路径依赖本质上反映了缺失的状态信息，并给出一个由 Hankel 算子秩刻画、可由短时导数恢复记忆“喷流”、从而把粗演化构造成精确自治系统的最小构造性补全方法，同时给出一般性的散度幂律标度结果、以及用于发现隐藏预测坐标的有限样本奇异值判据与反事实预测状态的识别准则。

title: Detector-Frame Quantum Limits for Heterodyne Timing in Relativistic Optical Links
abstract: Long-baseline optical links for space interferometry and satellite quantum networks rely on heterodyne phase tracking under Doppler motion and gravitational frequency shifts. These relativistic shifts can generate large detector-frame beat-frequency offsets over finite readout windows and thereby constrain the temporal precision of front-end phase readout. We develop a detector-frame framework for this problem using an effective two-mode signal--local-oscillator model in which relativistic motion rescales the local-oscillator frequency. Within this setting we derive closed-form Mandelstam--Tamm and Margolus--Levitin bounds for representative Gaussian resources and connect global state distinguishability with the operational precision of heterodyne phase tracking. In the bright-local-oscillator regime we identify a geometric--operational mismatch: the joint optical state can evolve on arbitrarily short global timescales while the relevant information rate is set by the measured detector record. Combining this result with an open-loop transient-acquisition analysis, we show that white phase noise and relativistic beat-frequency drift that is approximately constant over the acquisition window generate a cube-root scaling benchmark for the optimal pre-lock open-loop integration window and the minimum residual phase error. These results establish detector-frame benchmarks for quantum-limited heterodyne timing in relativistic optical links and clarify how global dynamical bounds enter task-restricted continuous optical measurements.

summaries.en: The paper develops a detector-frame theory of heterodyne phase-timing in relativistic optical links, deriving Mandelstam–Tamm and Margolus–Levitin bounds that connect global state distinguishability to achievable precision and showing that detector-record-limited information yields cube-root optimal scaling for open-loop integration under white phase noise and quasi-constant relativistic beat-frequency drift.
summaries.zh: 本文基于检测器坐标系建立了相对论光链路中异相探测的相位定时理论，推导了Mandelstam–Tamm与Margolus–Levitin界限，将全局态可区分性与可实现的精度关联起来，并表明在白相位噪声与相对论拍频在采集窗内近似常数的条件下，由探测器记录限制的信息速率会导致开环积分的最优时间尺度与剩余相位误差呈立方根标度。

title: On the Fast Electrons-Optical Modes Interaction Problem Error
abstract: A recently developed relativistic quantum optics approach for a fast electron beam-optical modes interaction problem (Optica 6, 1524--1534 (2019)) contains suggestion about a smallness of the error induced by replacement $\Psi_{\vec k}\approx\Psi_{\vec k_0}$ for noninteracting free electron Dirac spinors at such wave vector $\vec k$ that $\left|\vec k-\vec k_0 \right| \ll\left|\vec k_0\right|$ with $\vec k_0$ as a peaked wave vector of a focused electron beam. Here, based on quantum information approach we strictly investigated a degree of coincidence of spinors $\Psi_{\vec k}$ and $\Psi_{\vec k_0}$ by calculating fidelity for them. The analytical expression is obtained. It is shown that the fidelity inevitably depends on not only wave vectors $\vec k$ and $\vec k_0$ but also on mutual orientation of $[\vec k_0,\vec k]$ and $\hat{\vec{s}}^{\dagger}\vec{\sigma}\hat{\vec{s}}$ with $\vec{s}$ is a two-component spin unit vector and $\vec{\sigma}$ is a vector of Pauli matrices. This result can be conceived as a chirality-like effect in the fidelity and constraints spin arbitrariness when applying the developed relativistic quantum optics approach to the problems of interest. A geometrical configuration of $\vec k_0$, $\vec k-\vec k_0$, and $\hat{\vec{s}}^†\vec\sigma\hat{\vec{s}}$ that is optimal in terms of fidelity is established.
subjects: Quantum Physics (quant-ph) ; Mesoscale and Nanoscale Physics (cond-mat.mes-hall)

summaries.en: The paper uses a quantum-information fidelity calculation to strictly quantify the error in replacing Dirac spinors Ψ_k with Ψ_k0 in a relativistic quantum optics fast-electron/optical-mode interaction model, showing the fidelity depends on both the wave-vector difference and their geometric orientation relative to a spin/chirality-like operator and identifying an optimal spatial configuration for minimal error.
summaries.zh: 本文用量子信息中的保真度计算严格评估在相对论量子光学快电子与光学模相互作用模型中用 Ψ_k≈Ψ_k0 近似所引入的误差，结果表明保真度不仅取决于波矢 k 与 k0 之间的差，还取决于两者及自旋相关算符之间的相对几何取向（呈类似手性效应），并给出了使保真度最优的几何构型以约束该方法的适用自旋自由度。

title: How long is a photon?
abstract: A photon has the strange property that it travels along a null interval with zero proper time, hence its emission and absorption points are, in a sense, a singular event. For their part, the emission and absorption processes have a finite duration which determines the spectral content of the photon. The question in the title points to the conceptual difficulty in `stitching' together these three intervals, which all correspond to the same physical entity but have fundamentally incompatible temporal descriptions. A previously developed model for quantum wavefunction propagation solves this apparent dilemma by formulating the life cycle of a photon in terms of recursive Fourier transforms on dual spaces. Because it doesn't treat space as dependent on time, and it is built on the Fourier transform whose phase is an invariant in special relativity as well as the foundation of the uncertainty principle, the model is a promising candidate framework for making quantum mechanics compatible with relativity. The model proposes to serve as an improved Klein-Gordon equation, or relativistically compatible replacement for Schrödinger's equation.

summaries.en: The paper argues that modeling a photon's “zero proper time” null propagation together with finite emission/absorption durations leads to incompatible temporal descriptions, and it claims a recursive dual-space Fourier-transform wavefunction framework can reconcile them while offering a relativistically compatible, Klein–Gordon–like replacement for Schrödinger’s equation.
summaries.zh: 本文认为，在同时描述光子的“零固有时”类光传播与具有有限持续时间的发射/吸收过程时会出现时间表述上的不兼容问题，而作者提出一种基于双空间递归傅里叶变换的波函数传播模型可将其调和，并且该模型有望提供与相对论兼容的、类似克莱因–戈尔登方程的施行替代而非仅依赖薛定谔方程。

title: Hamiltonian-Dependent Compressibility and Physical Preservation in Approximate Quantum Compilation using Tensor Networks
abstract: Approximate quantum compilation (AQC) using tensor networks provides a promising route to reducing the circuit resources required for quantum simulation. However, the factors governing the compressibility of many-body dynamics and the extent to which compressed circuits retain physically relevant information on quantum hardware remain poorly understood. We investigate these questions using AQCtensor for an 80-qubit one-dimensional anisotropic XYZ Heisenberg chain initialized in a Néel state. By varying the exchange anisotropy and external magnetic field, we find that compression performance changes systematically with the anisotropic coupling configuration and field orientation. These variations are strongly associated with a nested-commutator measure related to second-order Trotter error, with corresponding directional trends also reflected in the target-state MPS bond dimension. For an 80-qubit quantum-hardware evaluation, AQCtensor compresses a 10-repetition target evolution to 5 repetitions while retaining a target-state fidelity of 0.995474, reducing the total circuit depth by 45.9% and the two-qubit gate count by 47.6%. The compressed circuit exhibits comparable behavior across magnetization, nearest-neighbor correlation, and Hamiltonian expectation measurements, while process-level diagnostics and local reduced-state tomography provide complementary characterization beyond these observables. Together, these results link AQCtensor compressibility to Hamiltonian commutator structure and target-state complexity and demonstrate substantial circuit reduction while retaining physically relevant features in an 80-qubit quantum-hardware experiment.

summaries.en: The paper studies how AQCtensor’s tensor-network-based approximate quantum compilation compresses an 80-qubit anisotropic XYZ Heisenberg chain and finds that compressibility depends systematically on Hamiltonian anisotropy and field orientation through a nested-commutator (second-order Trotter error) metric, enabling a 5×/2× reduction in repetitions and roughly halving circuit depth and two-qubit gate count while preserving high target-state fidelity and physical observables with process and tomography diagnostics beyond simple measurements.
summaries.zh: 本文研究了AQCtensor基于张量网络的近似量子编译如何压缩一个80量子比特各向异性XYZ海森伯链，发现其可压缩性会随哈密顿量的各向异性与外磁场方向系统变化，并可由与二阶Trotter误差相关的嵌套对易子度量来解释；在80量子硬件评估中，该方法将10次目标演化压缩为5次，在保留高目标态保真度的同时将电路深度与双量子门数量分别降低约45.

title: Compass in the Mirror: Quantum Backpropagation with the Hopf Ansatz
abstract: A variational quantum state may have many control angles, and its complete gradient contains one derivative for each. The task is to turn access to selected derivatives into a shared finite-shot record for the complete vector. The Hopf ansatz supplies the setting: it constructs any normalized pure state from nested two-way magnitude splits and, for complex states, leaf phases, with one directly programmed angle per split or phase. Earlier Hopf constructions prepare the state, recover coordinates from known amplitudes, and provide indexed derivative access. With a phase-calibrated controlled reflection, the inverse Hopf frame maps each normalized magnitude direction to a computational label, so every all-$X$ outcome contributes to every magnitude derivative. A separate signed leaf record supplies the complex phase block. A checkpoint variant reverses only the suffix below a selected depth and returns that layer's gradient block. For a complete chart with $M$ real-valued parameters, sufficient execution counts are $\mathcal{O}(\log\log M)$ for the global method and $\mathcal{O}(\log M\log\log M)$ for the complete checkpoint schedule at fixed additive coordinate accuracy and confidence. The global saving is record reuse, not a reduction of the $M$-entry output. Under the designated direct-angle schedules, the global method's assigned Hopf CNOT work and input/output-inclusive storage have at most logarithmic overhead relative to a matched scalar evaluation. The same Hopf geometry thus carries a state forward and the objective's complete coordinate response backward.

summaries.en: The paper proposes a Hopf-ansatz-based quantum backpropagation method that reuses a shared finite-shot record to obtain the complete gradient vector from selected derivative access, using phase-calibrated controlled reflections and a signed phase readout, with a checkpoint variant that reverses only part of the Hopf circuit and achieves execution counts of O(log log M) globally and O(log M log log M) for the full checkpoint schedule at fixed accuracy and confidence.
summaries.zh: 论文提出一种基于 Hopf 反变换（Hopf ansatz）的量子反向传播方法：通过相位校准的受控反射与带符号的相位读出，将共享的有限次测量记录复用起来，在仅访问部分导数的情况下仍可得到完整梯度向量；同时给出仅回溯所选深度以下后缀的检查点变体，在固定精度与置信度下全局方法所需执行次数为 O(log log M)，而完整检查点调度为 O(log M log log M)。

title: Below-threshold execution of fault-tolerant ripple-carry addition on a trapped-ion quantum computer
abstract: We deploy a universal fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) architecture based on error-detecting $[\![8,3,2]\!]$ and $[\![4,2,2]\!]$ codes on Quantinuum's Helios-1 trapped-ion quantum computer. We compile and execute ripple-carry adder (RCA) circuits for classical inputs up to five bits on this architecture. Uncomputing a workspace qubit provides an additional ``algorithmic check'' to detect errors. While available at both the physical and logical levels, this check synergizes with our architecture by increasing the effective fault distance of many circuit locations from two to four. Combining this algorithmic check with the error-detecting codes, we observed only a single logical failure in one-bit addition after burst-error filtering, yielding an estimated logical failure rate of $(6.0 \pm 5.9) \times 10^{-5}$. This is well below the $(3.5 \pm 1.3) \times 10^{-3}$ failure probability observed for one-bit addition on the same hardware in unencoded form. Two- and three-bit adders also showed performance improvements, while the longer four- and five-bit adders executed just above threshold.

title: Fast continuous ion transport through X-junctions with low motional excitation for QCCD architectures
abstract: Trapped ion quantum computing based on the quantum charge coupled device (QCCD) architecture uses functional zoning and ion transport to enable high fidelity computation and all to all qubit connectivity. As trapped ion quantum processing units (QPU) scale, 90° X-junction turns account for an increasing fraction of total transport time. Frequent junction crossings, therefore, make transport speed and final phonon excitation direct determinants of quantum algorithm execution efficiency. However, complex electric fields in X-junctions complicate waveform design, making it difficult to achieve high speed and low final phonon excitation simultaneously. Here, we develop a waveform design method for low-phonon-excitation high-speed X-junction(LHX-T) transport.
